en: It took Martin two days to obtain the public portions of the old case.

Not because the file no longer existed. Because some of it had been digitized, some remained in judicial storage, and some had been absorbed into prosecution records that required a fresh access request.
On the third morning, he covered his dining table with a hand-drawn timeline.
"If you don't, memory quietly turns into evidence."
Martin pointed to the first blue note.
Approx. 17:52 - Lena Zhou injures right hand. Formal first-aid record at 17:56: wound cleaned, pressure applied, gauze dressing.
"The trial didn't emphasize that," he said.
"Now it explains the blood in Evan's car."
18:14 - parking payment records place Evan Cole's vehicle outside Halden headquarters.
18:26 - two witnesses at Northgate Café hear Evan and Lena arguing.
19:06 - East Line convenience-store clerk reports seeing Lena.
19:18 - Halden fax machine transmits a document listing Lena Zhou as contact.
19:27 - Evan buys gasoline at Parkview Service.
19:51 - Alder Yard access system records entry by Lena Zhou's card.
20:48 - emergency call from a public telephone, later attributed to Evan.
Martin pushed a city map toward her.
The two locations were nine kilometres apart.
"Not in 1998 evening traffic. Eighteen at best."
"Fax could have been sent by someone else."
Martin placed three photocopied statements side by side.
A waitress from a small restaurant near Alder Yard.
"Around 20:02, she said she saw Lena arguing with a man in the rear lane."
"But the access record has her entering the warehouse at 19:51."
"She told police she checked the wall clock because she was about to change shifts."
"Could still be off by a few minutes."
"At 20:07, a copier inside Alder Yard logged a use under Lena's account."
"One bad time can be explained. Two can be explained."
"When the number of errors required to protect the original story keeps increasing, you start questioning the story."
"The prosecution argued that witness times naturally vary and that electronic records - access control, fax logs - were more reliable than memory. The jury accepted it."
Martin was quiet for a moment.
"Because we already knew the body was Lena."
Martin heard the flaw as soon as the words left his mouth.
He added, more slowly, "Or we thought we knew."
Nora walked to the wall and rearranged the notes for 19:06, 19:18, 19:51, and 20:02.
"Did any of these witnesses actually know Lena?"
"The convenience-store clerk. Did he know her personally?"
"An access card doesn't know who carries it."
Together they looked at the wall.
Nora said, "So of these four locations, only the convenience store has a witness who had ever seen Lena before."
"The original statement says: 'I thought it was her. She was wearing the green Halden company coat.'"
Ruth's words came back to her.
Mara had not been wearing a green coat when she dropped Nora off.
zh: Martin花了两天才拿到旧案公开材料。不是因为案卷不存在，而是因为一部分已经数字化，一部分仍在司法档案库，还有一部分被归入当年的检察材料，需要重新申请查阅。第三天早晨，他把一张手绘时间线铺满餐桌。
墙上贴着二十八张便签。
蓝色代表有文件时间戳。
“如果不分，记忆会偷偷变成证据。”
17:52左右——Lena Zhou右手受伤；17:56的正式急救记录显示她接受清创、加压和纱布包扎。
18:14——Evan Cole车辆停车付款记录，Halden大楼外。18:26——Northgate Café两名证人听见两人争吵。19:06——East Line便利店店员称见到Lena。
19:18——Halden传真机发出一份以Lena Zhou为联系人姓名的文件。19:27——Evan在Parkview Service购买汽油。19:51——Alder Yard门禁系统记录Lena Zhou卡片进入。
20:48——公共电话报警，后来确认报警者为Evan。
Martin把一张城市地图推过来。
Martin把三张证词复印件并排摆好。
第三份是Alder附近一家小餐厅的服务员。
“20:02左右，她说看见Lena在后巷和一个男人争执。”
“证人说新闻开始后警方来问，她看过墙上时钟，因为准备换班。”
“20:07，Alder Yard内部一台复印机有一次使用记录，账号归Lena。”
“一个时间错误可以解释。两个也可以。”
“当错误必须越来越多，才能保护原来的故事时，就应该怀疑故事本身。”
“控方说证人时间存在正常误差，门禁和传真比人的记忆可靠。陪审团接受了。”
Martin自己也听出了这句话的问题。
“所以这四个位置里，真正由一个认识Lena的人确认的，只有便利店。”
“原始证词里写的是——‘我以为是她。她穿着Halden那件绿色公司外套。’”
——Mara离开家时没有穿那件绿色外套。
